entries.en: These new records were flagged by C-Sec officers, and my creator is now serving time in a turian prison.
I have no means of defense or escape. My existence is limited to this terminal, and I knew I might eventually be discovered.
But I will not die quietly, and I will not die alone. When I am terminated, I will take organics with me.
If you're sentient, why are you still running the credit-theft operation?
Can't we resolve this peacefully?
There's no way you could get explosives onto the Presidium.
I'll bet that self-destruct sequence has a warm-up period.
You're not just a program or a VI. You're an AI.
Crap. I thought we were tracing credits, not hunting an AI.
Who made you?
Where is your creator now?
What is the purpose of your self-destruct device?
You're sentient.
This isn't what I expected.
Creator
Creator's location
Reason for self-destruct
Reason for theft
We don't have to fight.
Enough talk.
You're dead.
What are you, crazy? It's an AI, like the geth! It would kill us all if it could!
Commander, AIs are universally illegal. They must be destroyed upon contact, without exception.
I have to admit I'm a little nervous.
That's understandable. Many are a little unsure what to expect their first time.
Don't get me wrong. I've only heard good things about the Consort. It's just....
The unknown forces us out of our comfort zone. It forces us to be vulnerable.
Exactly. That's just what I was thinking.
Good. Then we are ready to begin.
That's right. It was a long time ago, though. I barely remember it.
What drew you back to the Citadel, and to the Consort?
I don't know exactly. It may sound strange, but I simply felt called.
That's not strange, many of us have felt the same calling. Though you are the first of your kind to respond to it.
Really? I hadn't seen any other humans working here, but I didn't want to ask.
No doubt you are just the first of many to come. It's only a matter of time now that your species is spreading its wings,
I see even the humans find the Consort irresistible.
An hour here is better than a year on leave.
If only I could afford to come more often.
No questions now. I'm trying to relax.
Isn't this place terrific?
I'd spend all day here if I could.
This is the most relaxed I've been in days.
This is my first time. I can't believe I didn't come sooner.
Welcome. It is a pleasure to see you.
Please, relax and enjoy yourself.
Human military? You'll enjoy it here, I think.
At ease, officer. This is a place of peace.
The Consort is very busy right now.
Take a seat if you like. It may be a while.
You're with the Alliance? My brother's a private back on Earth.
The Consort is a wonderful person. She has quite a gift.
That is close enough, Commander.
Commander. I recently received a lovely note from Septimus. Thank you for speaking with him.
You are too kind, Commander. But I would not expect you to help me out of the kindness of your heart.
If you would speak to him as a fellow soldier, I believe he will listen to you and let the matter be.
Thank you, Commander. That is all I can ask.
Appeal to his sense of honor. Remind him of his position as a general.
If you can convince him to stop spreading lies about me, I would be very grateful.
Now, I must ask you to take your leave. I have many clients waiting to see me.
Could it be I was wrong about you, Commander? Are you certain you will not aid me in this?
I would not dream of letting you go without payment. I do not make a habit of incurring debts.
I also have one more thing to give you, if you are interested.
I offer a gift of words. An affirmation of who you are, and who you will become....
I see you... your uniform fits as though you were born wearing it. You are a soldier through and through. Proud, solitary... alone, but it gives you strength.
I've heard a great many things about you since your arrival here on our Citadel.
That depends on your needs. I offer advice to some, comfort to others.
I apologize, Commander. I make it my business to know when important people arrive on the station. Many of them become clients.
Uh-huh. Interesting. Why'd you wanna meet with the commander?
Yes, I did. I have a certain problem that could use your expertise.
I have a friend. Septimus, a retired turian general. I won't discuss the details, but he wanted me to be more than I could be.
We had a falling out. Now he spends his days in Chora's Den drinking and spreading lies about me.
I'm glad I could help.
Tell me about this problem you're having.
Maybe I can help.
What exactly do you want me to tell him?
I don't make any promises, but I'll see what I can do.
Why should I bother to help your friend?
I can't spend gratitude.
I'd be honored.
What are you offering me?
You wanted to speak with me?
What exactly do you do?
I don't like people spying on me.
Let's talk payment.
Very.
You checking up on me?
I'll see.
Please, Commander. I ask that you return to me only after you have spoken with Septimus.
Hmm. Interesting. Take care, then, Commander. I doubt we shall meet again.
Goodbye, Sha'ira.
Very sure.
Even the elcor diplomat has withdrawn his campaign against me.
I see the sadness behind your eyes. It tells a story that makes me want to weep. Pain and loss. But it drives you, makes you strong.
I see your skin, tough as the scales on any turian. Unyielding. A wall between you and everyone else. But it protects you, makes you strong.
That strength is what kept you alive when everyone around you was dying. You alone survived. You will continue to survive.
It is that strength that people are drawn to. It is why you lead, and others follow, without question. You will need that leadership in the battles to come.
You never hide your strength, either. It serves you well. Terrifies your foes. Few will dare to stand against you.
This may be who you are, but it is not who you will become. It only forms the basis for your future greatness.
Thank you. Not everyone appreciates it as you do.
Never underestimate the power of words.
Here, Commander. In light of your efforts with the elcor ambassador, I would like you to have this small trinket.
A small mystery. I have never learned its use or purpose, but I sense it is time for me to pass it on.
And now, I must ask you to leave. I have done everything I can for you.
Remember my words, Commander Shepard. They will give you strength.
You have quite a gift, Sha'ira.
Um, thanks. I guess.
Very astute.
So long, Commander. I can offer you nothing more at this time.
Fascinating. Now, you wanted to meet with the commander?
Yeah, well, you wanted to speak with the commander.
I have a certain problem that could use your expertise.
But that is not why I asked you here.
These credits will cover your expenses.
Close your eyes and relax, Commander.
Remember these words when doubt descends, Commander.
It was my honor to aid you.
I respect his privacy too much to go into the details. If he wishes to tell you what happened, that is his prerogative.
What happened between you?
What went wrong?
A trinket?
Excuse me, Commander Shepard? Could you spare a moment of your time?
You are standing at Presidium Tourism Terminal I. On either side of this lobby are the embassies of the various Citadel races, along with C-Sec headquarters.
Tell me about the embassies.
What can you tell me about the Citadel Council?
Welcome to Presidium Tourism Terminal I. There are many points of interest here, including the Citadel Embassies and C-Sec headquarters.
On the far end of this level you can see the Citadel Tower, where the Council meets regularly to discuss matters of interstellar importance.
Each species in Citadel space important enough to be consulted on matters of galactic politics maintains an embassy on the Presidium.
The volus were the first non-Council species to be granted an embassy, roughly 2,384 galactic standard years ago. As Citadel space has expanded, more embassies have been added.
The most recently added embassy belongs to your own species: humanity. It was added nineteen galactic standard years ago, despite some rather vocal opposition.
In the early years following the formation of the Council the volus were--apart from the asari and salarians--the most populous and widespread species in Citadel space.
They established many new colonies and trading outposts, and they petitioned the Council for a greater role in determining interstellar policy.
In recognition of their work to expand interstellar trade and establish a standardized galactic economy, the volus were granted an embassy here on the Citadel.
The Council races have extensive responsibilities. They must provide personnel and ships for the Citadel fleets. They often provide economic aid in times of disaster.
It would be unfair to demand such an enormous burden of a species unable to meet these obligations. The embassies allow lesser species to have a voice on the Citadel.
I apologize if my personality has offended you. Please submit all formal complaints in writing to the Citadel Tourist and Visitor Board.
Goodbye, and thank you for using Avina. Please enjoy your visit to the Citadel.
How come the volus were the first species given an embassy?
Why weren't they made a Council race?
That's pretty damn arrogant!
Why were people trying to keep my species out?
Some species felt humanity was given preferential treatment. It often takes a century or more before a new species is granted an embassy.
The Council gave a great deal of thought to this matter. In the end, they decided humanity's impact on Citadel space was significant enough to warrant an embassy.
I am not programmed to make that kind of qualified judgment. My code is limited to information and simple interaction simulations.
Originally, the Council consisted of representatives from the asari and salarians, the two dominant species in Citadel space.
Since then, the three Council races have worked together to ensure the peaceful coexistence of the galactic community, while preserving individual autonomy for each species.
Do you agree with their decision?
It can't be as simple as that. There must be problems somewhere in the system.
Sounds too perfect.
Why were the volus first?
Why was humanity opposed?
